kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: the near-floor control must self-negate — zero unique detections against the sampled review

overlapping rules in an extracted table outside DMN-analyzer ingest; the rule-lens witness class is a named overlap finding under the extracted-table scope
a shadowed rule in an extracted table outside DMN-analyzer ingest; the rule-lens witness class is a named shadow finding under the extracted-table scope
a derivable rule in an extracted table outside DMN-analyzer ingest; the rule-lens witness class is a named derivable finding under the extracted-table scope
floor control — at the near-floor table the conventional scripted review catches every injected fault; the probe must show zero unique detections here (design Decision 2 / rule-lens precedent)

commands: python3 prototype/rule_lens_extracted_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: 7 faults, 4 unique detections (baseline arm frozen)
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- rules fixtures/probes/rule_lens/floor/cct-1492-15.ct.json --values fecha=2024-10-01 --max-candidates 8 --json  # exit 0, findings []
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- rules fixtures/probes/rule_lens/floor/faults/01-gap-remove-row.ct.json --values fecha=2024-10-01 --max-candidates 8 --json  # exit 6, 1 finding [underconstraint]
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- rules fixtures/probes/rule_lens/floor/faults/02-overlap-different-cap.ct.json --values fecha=2024-10-01 --max-candidates 8 --json  # exit 3, 1 finding [violation]

witness.question: which action applies? no rule covers this input class

comparison.conventional_baseline: The sampled review asserts the single printed cap at fecha=2024-10-01; dropping the only rule fails the assertion and the second injected rule makes the cell ambiguous under DeclaredDisjoint — both faults are caught, so the lens buys nothing here.

discrepancies: Source scope: the annex PDF is not in the bogart corpus read surface (corpus_attachments empty; the exact values appear on 0 serving pages) — the grounded artifact is a recon text extraction, recorded here so no corpus-level claim is implied.
procedure: 1. The extracted table, its provenance (annex text sha256), the fault set, and the sampled conventional review were committed in fixtures/probes/rule_lens/ before any run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/rule_lens_extracted_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: the review a team performs on an extracted table — a sampled (scope, date) value check resolved under the document's declared policy, four of six cells above the floor and the single floor cell.
3. The probe arm ran `catherine rules` over the declared finite domain on the same fault documents; findings are the CLI's verbatim output.
4. A fault is caught only when the arm's output evidences it; unique detections are the lens findings on faults the sampled review missed (the rule-lens P8 comparison procedure, unchanged).
5. The verdict follows harness::derive_probe_verdict: zero unique = killed; unique with an executed baseline arm = survived.
